A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical-filtering and transformer study. All 18 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including figures, equations, references and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B report original transformer experiments on root classification, masked language modeling, attention patterns, ancestor probing and pretraining.

after.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix D retain original experiments and add probability-matching results, tests on other grammars and additional probing controls.

M1.justification: The non-overlapping tree generator, hierarchical filtering, single-head transformer architecture, task-specific readouts and cross-entropy objectives are retained. Moving model and architecture details to Appendices A–B and expanding the BP derivation do not establish a redesigned method.

E1.justification: The synthetic-tree domain and root-classification, MLM and ancestor-prediction tasks remain. v2 adds uniformly sampled input sequences as a distinct distribution-shift scenario for probability comparisons, beyond v1's tests across hierarchical-filtering levels (Figures 1(b) and 11).

E2.justification: v1 Figure 1(d) compares training from scratch with MLM pretraining followed by fine-tuning. v2 Figure 1(f) adds a frozen-encoder pretraining comparator alongside unfrozen fine-tuning and training from scratch. Matched and mismatched BP remain the principal reference methods.

E3.justification: v2 introduces full-output comparisons using KL divergence, prediction agreement and Spearman correlation, including comparisons against differently filtered BP oracles on identical inputs. It also adds frozen-encoder controls and probes trained only at the first and last positions but tested across all positions. Separately, the relocated MLM curve's caption changes P from 2^18 to 2^17 and incorrectly calls the task root prediction; this does not reliably establish an actual budget change.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained attention, filtering and layer-count analyses, v2 adds probability-level calibration diagnostics, robustness across three additional grammars (Figure 9), a frozen-encoder transfer control and a probe-position generalization test (Figure 14, left). These substantially expand checks of BP-like computation and alternative explanations for the probing results.

E5.justification: v2 identifies data-generation seed 0 for the main experiments and seeds 1, 15 and 31 for the additional grammars. v1 gives no specific seeds. These disclosures concern grammar realizations; neither version reports repeated-training run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds probability scatterplots, KL trajectories, prediction-agreement and ranking results, other-grammar scores, and frozen-encoder transfer results. Probing curves are revised and extended to the root: v1 describes accurate recovery one ancestry level beyond the probed layer, whereas v2 describes recovery up to the corresponding level. Most original classification and MLM accuracy results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds an explicit nested downward-BP expansion and a first-layer auxiliary-message base case (Equations 23–24) to the recursion already presented in v1 Appendix C. The core BP equations and transformer construction remain. v1's separate mathematical formulation of the broadcast-on-trees special case is removed.

C1.justification: v2 introduces spontaneous calibration of full predicted probability distributions, including on uniformly sampled inputs, as a central contribution. This extends v1's emphasis on matching BP prediction accuracy to a stronger scientific claim about computational correspondence. The hierarchical-learning and pretraining contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains sample-complexity differences through calibration and deterministic versus ambiguous labels, replacing v1's principal explanation based on weaker correlations and signal-to-noise ratio. It explicitly qualifies the BP construction as idealized rather than an exact account of learned computation, discusses probe confounding and random-input dispersion, and develops applicability boundaries and possible extensions.

D1.justification: A new Reproducibility Statement supplies a repository location and describes data-generation, transformer-training and BP implementations. Appendix D.6 newly specifies probe training on 2^14 sequences for 100 epochs, sharing across positions and the averaged cross-entropy objective. Existing optimizer, batch-size and learning-rate details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises research positioning: it removes the broadcast-on-trees subsection, adds layer-dependent production rules to the RHM comparison, and explicitly connects BP to inside-outside through Baker and Sato. It adds ambiguous-PCFG, curriculum-learning and biological-sequence connections. The Rende et al. reference also changes to a different work on distributional simplicity bias.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary are extensively rewritten. The experimental narrative is reorganized into learning in time and embedded computation, while detailed generator definitions, architecture equations and several analyses move to expanded appendices. This substantially changes the exposition and document structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned from four panels to six, introducing probability scatterplots and KL trajectories and redisplaying attention maps. Original accuracy panels become separate figures. Probing displays are split, extended and relabeled; several new diagnostic figures are added, and attention figures are resized and repositioned. These changes go well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1's central mechanistic interpretation relied heavily on accuracy matching and attention patterns. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence with full-probability comparisons, additional grammars and controls addressing probe artifacts, while clarifying the limits of its idealized construction. New reproduction instructions also improve inspectability. Some stale figure references and the inconsistent MLM caption remain, but these limited reporting defects do not outweigh the stronger support for the paper's central conclusions.
